text: We evaluated a method that measures per-sample loss drop over training as a learnability signal and applies adaptive label smoothing weighted by that signal, on the chat_preference testbed. The single reported metric is a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.62. Several important caveats limit what can be concluded from this. No baseline PGR was provided, so we cannot say whether this value represents an improvement over an existing or naive approach — the 0.62 figure stands alone and is uninterpretable as a gain. The configuration also reports no seed count (num_seeds is absent), so we have no information about run-to-run variance, and no standard error or confidence interval accompanies the point estimate. Results are furthermore confined to a single testbed, so generalization to other preference or classification settings is untested. The finding should therefore be read as a preliminary, single-number observation that motivates a properly seeded comparison against a stated baseline rather than as evidence that the learnability-weighted smoothing approach works.
